title: Continual soft-prompt then shared Mirror residual then private prompt escalation
dataset: WikiText-2 raw, sequential article tasks; train split for development tasks and test split for fresh tasks
hypothesis: A continual prompt system can preserve per-task held-out continuation quality by first sharing a common prompt, then adding rank-4 shared-basis task coordinates, and allocating private prompt residuals only when the frozen validation gate requires them; this should use fewer actual bytes than independent prompts while making escalation frequency explicit.
physical_object: Frozen Pythia-70M with eight sequentially learned 8-token virtual prompts
mirror_coordinate: Per-task rank-4 coordinate over the shared centered-PCA basis of prompt residuals around the current shared prompt mean
task_construction: For each bank, deterministically sample eight distinct WikiText articles with at least 2048 tokens. Fit each task prompt on article tokens 0:1024. Use four fixed 64-token windows from suffix tokens 1024:2048 for validation/evaluation. Process tasks in seeded order. The fresh bank uses only test.txt articles; it is not used for development choices.

prompt_training.optimizer: AdamW on prompt embeddings only; frozen Pythia weights
prompt_training.initialization: Gaussian std 0.02, seed derived deterministically from bank seed and task index

continual_encoding.order: seeded task order fixed before training
continual_encoding.shared_prompt: running mean of all prompt vectors seen so far
continual_encoding.basis: centered PCA of seen prompt residuals around the running mean; signs canonicalized by largest-magnitude loading
continual_encoding.recode_policy: After each task, recompute the seen-task shared basis/codes and re-evaluate retention for all seen tasks; report the cumulative re-encoding time.
continual_encoding.private_escalation: If rank-4 reconstruction is more than 0.05 nat/token worse than that task's independent full-prompt score on the fixed validation suffix, store the FP16 private prompt residual target-minus-decoded-prompt. The decoder adds this residual at inference.
controls: Mirror rank-4 codes plus rule-triggered private residual

development.selection: No hyperparameter sweep. Rank 4, 0.05 nat/token escalation threshold, prompt training schedule, and serialization are fixed by protocol. Report both development banks separately.

fresh.open_rule: Run all three fresh banks only after both registered development banks complete. Do not alter the frozen rule after inspecting fresh results.

storage.authority: actual uncompressed NPZ inference payload bytes after load/serialize round trip
storage.common_backbone: Report separately and exclude only from incremental prompt-bank comparisons; do not claim full-system bytes smaller than the frozen backbone.

compute.no_free_reconstruction: Charge basis decoding and private residual addition as inference compute.

primary_metrics: held-out next-token NLL delta versus independent prompt
old-task NLL drift after each new task
success_gate: Both development banks: escalation system is within +0.05 nat/token of independent prompts on every task, uses <=0.75x independent prompt bytes, and Mirror's bytes or quality strictly improves on the matched native rank-4 code control. Fresh banks are opened after this gate for confirmation.
decision_rule: Any quality or byte miss is FAIL. Exact equality with native rank-4 coding is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution, but continue the preregistered fresh screen if tiered private escalation itself meets both development quality and byte gates; report the tiering result separately from the Mirror claim.
boundaries: This is a small continual text-prompt bank screen, not broad continual-learning capacity evidence
Prompt residual escalation is an input-space private adapter surrogate, not a LoRA weight adapter
No task router is studied; task identity is supplied
A rank-4 code count is not independent functional capacity
Family MA-594 remains deferred under the existing MA-461/462 HyperFormer family diagnostic
